summary: deploy.sh: self-update from $RELEASE after git checkout, so repo changes to deploy.sh actually take effect
description:
vps-bootstrap.sh install -o deploy -g deploy /srv/guru-web/deploy.sh runs once at bootstrap. Subsequent changes to deploy/deploy.sh in the repo never reach the VPS — every CI deploy SSHes in and runs the bootstrap-era script. Today's symptom: PR #17's NEXT_PUBLIC_* env-source step and PR #23's self-heal chown both shipped to repo but never executed on the VPS, so the bundle still has empty publishableKey several deploys after the supposed fix.

Fix: after git fetch/checkout, compare $RELEASE/deploy/deploy.sh to the running script ($0). If they differ, cp it into place and exec the new one with the same SHA arg. The new script's first action is the same self-update check, which will now find the files identical and proceed normally — no infinite loop.

Done when:
- deploy.sh self-updates after git fetch/checkout, before npm ci.
- Self-update is idempotent (no-op when files match) and short-circuits via exec.
- Source-level test asserts the self-update block is present in deploy.sh and runs after fetch/before npm ci.
- README documents the self-update so operators don't reach for vps-bootstrap.sh again to push deploy.sh changes.

Operator unblock for the current incident: cp /srv/guru-web/releases/<latest>/deploy/deploy.sh /srv/guru-web/deploy.sh once by hand. After that, this PR's self-update keeps it current automatically.

resolution.note: Self-update via cmp + cp + exec after git fetch. One-time hand copy needed for the bootstrap-era version on existing VPSes; subsequent updates flow automatically.
